lesson_title: Potential Energy: The Bank Account in the Sky
hook_text: Every water tower is a savings account. Height is money. Here's the exchange rate.
clip_script: Every township water tower is a savings account. The pump spends electricity all night pushing water up — hard work, paid in full. But that spending is a deposit: the water sits up there holding the energy, and when you open a tap, the height pays it back as rushing pressure. That is gravitational potential energy — energy banked by lifting against gravity. The bill is E p equals m g h: mass times g is the weight, and weight times height is the lift's full cost. A 2 kilogram brick to a 5 metre scaffold: 2 times 9,8 times 5 — 98 joules, banked. And if it falls? Every joule pays out as speed. That is why building sites wear hard hats.
visual_style: Water tower drawn as a piggy bank on stilts; coins ride up with the water at night and pour out of a tap at dawn; a brick's till-slip prints 2 × 9,8 × 5 = 98 J.
pacing: Cosy water-tower open, coin-flow visual, snappy till-slip calculation, hard-hat sting.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and price any lift with three numbers.
